question: After a gated holder is killed before checking or writing, can one bounded contender retry preserve the same question/history/allowance and distinguish permission from mere lock release?
level: External finite receiving experiment; unchanged exact-rational arithmetic and SQLite receiver, not native semantics.
objects: One trusted local SQLite ledger and one accepted slot per episode. Two finite decision-checkpoint families; source probabilities, losses, histories, scale steps and original balanced allowance are fixed by the existing producer. The reuse instance changes the prior, kernel, loss and cost.
types_and_domain: Inherited strict JSON records, rational numerator/denominator pairs, bounded integer allowance grant=3 spent=2 remaining=1, history capacity four. Candidate profile remains adva.research.decision-ledger-contention.v0. No new candidate syntax or native identities.
quantifiers: Exactly four predetermined schedules: primary valid retry, asymmetric valid retry, primary false arithmetic retry, asymmetric changed-history context retry. Not exhaustive scheduling or arbitrary crash coverage.
method: Reuse unmodified contention producer, gate, receiver and six ancestor receivers. Pause holder after BEGIN IMMEDIATE readiness and before metadata/candidate reads. Contender must return pre-transaction LedgerBusy while holder is alive. SIGKILL only that owned child, reap it, then read full logical state. One explicitly budgeted retry follows; no release byte is sent and no second retry is permitted.
acceptance: Post-exit full schema and application rows equal the pre-state; valid retries independently check arithmetic and commit one slot/one debit. False arithmetic and changed receiver context are refused without a debit or logical mutation. No reply from killed holder is classified as a mathematical negative.
cost: Record construction, serialization, full-state observation and episode wall time, actual child lifetimes, finished receiver work plus holder work reported at the gate, and Linux peak RSS. Gate/OS/supervisor operations are not included in receiver work. No peak aggregate concurrent-memory claim.
protected: Complete receiver question, histories, exact arithmetic, fingerprints, original allowance and prior evidence
No native Close/free/Seal/M6, arithmetic universality, automatic fuel reset or external action
Additive-zero and multiplicative-one domains unchanged; no scalar value used as semantic identity
exit: Stop after four episodes or the first unexpected outcome/limit; keep raw partial evidence. At most one implementation correction with retained failed evidence. No waiting for CI as research.
residuals: Exit after writes or during COMMIT is not tested in an overlapping schedule
No power loss, storage tampering, external exactly-once, distributed safety or scheduler fairness
Successful publication and supplied assumptions do not establish human interpretation or practical decision benefit
